newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-RONALDO CROWNED KING OF SOCCER BY FIFA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RONALDO CROWNED KING OF SOCCER BY FIFA.

text.p: Barcelona's young Brazilian star Ronaldo, who has taken the Spanish league by storm in his first season, was crowned FIFA world player of the year on Monday.
The 20-year-old received more than double the points of his nearest rival, last year's winner George Weah of AC Milan, in a poll of more than 100 international soccer coaches.
England captain Alan Shearer of Newcastle was third in the run-off which featured three of the soccer world's top marksmen.
The Brazilian, top scorer in the Spanish league with 15 goals this season, received 329 points under the poll's system of voting, against 140 for Weah and 123 for Shearer.
The award, the sixth time it has been made, was presented to Ronaldo at a glittering ceremony later on Monday in Lisbon's Belem Cultural Centre.

Ronaldo is the second Brazilian to win the award after Romario was acclaimed the world's best player in 1994. Other past winners are Italy's Roberto Baggio, Dutchman Marco Van Basten and Lothar Matthaeus of Germany.

The Brazilian, regarded by many as the most exciting player to emerge since Argentina's Diego Maradona, is so highly prized by Barcelona that they recently bound him to the club for 10 years with a multi-million dollar contract.
Dubbed the "extra-terrestrial" by soccer-mad Spanish fans, the shaven-haired Ronaldo made an explosive start to the season with Barcelona.
He likes nothing better than to latch on to the ball in midfield and head for goal, his extraordinary balance and strength enabling him to appear to bounce off defenders.
His modesty has also won him admirers beyond the massed ranks of Barcelona supporters.

"I am young and I still have a lot to learn," he told a news conference after the award ceremony. "When they handed me the trophy, I remembered when I was young and how I wanted to be the best player in the world."
The biggest ovation of the night was for Liberia's George Weah, whose attendance at the ceremony was in doubt up to the last moment.

Weah received a special FIFA award for fair-play and the audience burst into prolonged applause when the African star handed over a one million escudo ($6,000) cheque to be donated to a society for the protection of children.

The Liberian nearly did not make the trip to Lisbon because he faces a court action for damages in Portugal after Porto defender Jorge Costa's nose was broken in an incident at the end of a bad-tempered European Cup league match between the Portuguese champions and AC Milan last November.

Weah, who says he was severely provoked by Costa, feared legal problems and a hostile reception in Lisbon and FIFA were unable to confirm his presence until only hours before the ceremony was due to begin.
"The (fair play) award is an honour not just for Liberia but for the whole of the African continent," Weah said.
